evidence: src/application/use-cases/StartSubscription.ts: execute() reaches storage only through the injected ports SubscriptionRepository.activeFor, nextId and save, and PlanCatalog.find. It contains no persistence implementation.
src/application/use-cases/StartSubscription.ts: Subscription.start(...) hands creating the aggregate to the domain model.
src/application/use-cases/StartSubscription.ts: summarise(subscription, plan) maps the result to an application-layer DTO (SubscriptionSummary).

src/application/use-cases/StartSubscription.ts: The seat check (`!Number.isInteger(seats) || seats < 1`) and the duplicate-plan check run before the work and use the domain SubscriptionError. They are borderline but acceptable checks for a use case.
The file has no HTTP, framework or transport concerns. The controller lives separately in src/infrastructure/http/SubscriptionController.ts.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is a typical application-layer use case. StartSubscription.execute coordinates the work: it checks the input, looks up the plan through the PlanCatalog port, checks existing subscriptions through the SubscriptionRepository port, has the domain factory Subscription.start build the aggregate, saves it through the port, and maps the result to an application DTO with summarise. It has no persistence, transport or framework code: no SQL, no HTTP and no framework types. Saving goes only through domain ports that are injected. Two checks are borderline. First, the seat-count check (a whole number, at least 1) could arguably be an invariant that belongs inside Subscription.start. Second, the check that a customer does not already hold the same plan is a rule that looks across several subscriptions. Use cases often do both kinds of check before doing the work. They use domain error types, and the aggregate may enforce the same rules itself. There is no ADR text saying these rules must live only in the domain, so I don't count them as clearly misplaced. Every responsibility in the file fits the application layer's coordinating role.
